**3.0 CONFIRMATION OF MINUTES OF THE PREVIOUS MEETING**

The minutes of the Board meeting held on 12 December 2023 were circulated to all members prior to this meeting. The minutes were reviewed and confirmed as a true and accurate record of the proceedings of that meeting. The Chairman signed the minutes as confirmed.

**4.0 MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES**

**4.1** The Treasurer reported that the outstanding payment to the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company for the 2023 dry-season fertilizer order had been settled on 28 December 2023. The payment of ₦4,850,000.00 was made via bank transfer, and the receipt has been filed.

**4.2** The Secretary reported that letters of appreciation had been dispatched to the three cooperative societies that hosted the Board’s inspection visits in November 2023. No further action was required.

**4.3** The Chairman noted that the matter of the proposed borehole rehabilitation at the Dambatta collection centre had been deferred to this meeting for discussion under Item 7.0. There was no other business arising.

**5.0 CHAIRMAN’S REMARKS**

According to the board minutes, Ahmadu Bello appointment_date is 2024-01-15. Record status: current.

The Chairman welcomed members to the first Board meeting of the year. He noted that the 2024 farming season would be critical for the Federation, given the anticipated increase in the cost of inputs and the ongoing efforts to expand the Federation’s warehouse capacity. He urged members to consider the budget proposals for the year carefully and to prioritise programmes that would directly benefit member cooperatives.

**6.0 APPROVAL OF THE 2024 BUDGET**

The Treasurer presented the draft budget for the year ending 31 December 2024. He highlighted the following key figures:

- Total projected income: ₦128,650,000.00
- Total projected expenditure: ₦121,400,000.00
- Projected surplus: ₦7,250,000.00

The budget provided for an allocation of ₦35,000,000.00 for the procurement of fertiliser and improved seeds, ₦18,200,000.00 for the construction of a new warehouse at the Challawa centre, and ₦9,500,000.00 for the Federation’s tractor hire programme. The budget also made provision for administrative expenses of ₦12,750,000.00.

Members raised questions regarding the provision for staff training, which had been set at ₦1,500,000.00. The Treasurer explained that this amount was intended to cover two training workshops for cooperative extension officers. After discussion, the Board approved the budget as presented.

**Resolution 2024/01:** *That the budget for the year ending 31 December 2024, with total projected income of ₦128,650,000.00 and total projected expenditure of ₦121,400,000.00, be and is hereby approved.*

**7.0 REPORT ON THE DAMBATTA COLLECTION CENTRE BOREHOLE**

The General Manager, Ahmadu Bello, presented a verbal report on the condition of the borehole at the Dambatta collection centre. He informed the Board that the borehole had been non-functional since October 2023 due to a failed pump. A quotation for the replacement of the pump and associated works, in the sum of ₦2,350,000.00, had been obtained from a reputable contractor in Kano. The General Manager recommended that the work be carried out before the onset of the rainy season to ensure water availability for the cleaning of storage facilities.
**8.0 APPOINTMENT OF HEAD OF PLANNING**

The Chairman informed the Board that the position of Head of Planning, which had been vacant since the retirement of Alhaji Musa Ibrahim in March 2024, had been advertised internally and externally. He reported that the Interview Panel, chaired by the Vice-Chairman, had considered applications from eleven candidates and had shortlisted four for interview.

The Vice-Chairman presented the panel’s report. He stated that all four shortlisted candidates had been interviewed on 27 May 2024 and that the panel had assessed each candidate against the criteria of relevant experience, knowledge of cooperative law and practice, and familiarity with the Federation’s operational areas. After deliberation, the panel recommended the appointment of Fatima Sani, who had served as Senior Planning Officer in the Federation since 2019 and had acted as Head of Planning during the vacancy.

The Board discussed the recommendation at length. The Treasurer noted that Fatima Sani had demonstrated strong capability in preparing the 2024 budget submissions and in coordinating the Federation’s input distribution schedules. The General Manager supported the recommendation, stating that she had managed the planning unit effectively during the period of the vacancy and had maintained good working relationships with the zonal officers.

The board minutes state that Fatima Sani appointment_date is 2024-06-01. Record status: current. There being no further nominations, the Chairman put the matter to a vote.

**Resolution 2024/02:** *That Fatima Sani be and is hereby appointed as Head of Planning of the Kano River Basin Cooperative Federation with effect from 1 June 2024, subject to the satisfactory completion of a six-month probationary period.*

The Chairman congratulated the appointee and asked the General Manager to ensure that the necessary letter of appointment, including the terms and conditions of service, be issued before the effective date.

**9.0 OPERATIONAL UPDATE ON FERTILISER PROCUREMENT**

The General Manager reported that the Federation had received confirmation from the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company regarding the allocation of fertiliser for the 2024 farming season. The allocation comprised 1,200 metric tonnes of NPK 20:10:10 and 800 metric tonnes of urea. The total cost, including transport to the Federation’s central store in Kano, was estimated at ₦214,000,000.00, which was within the budget provision of ₦35,000,000.00 only in respect of the Federation’s own procurement share; the remainder was to be financed through the Central Bank of Nigeria’s commercial agricultural credit scheme, for which the Federation had already submitted the necessary documentation.

The General Manager further informed the Board that the disbursement of the loan was expected within three weeks. He recommended that the Federation proceed with the engagement of transport contractors for the movement of fertiliser from the central store to the zonal collection centres at Dambatta, Challawa, and Tudun Wada. The Board noted the update.

**10.0 REPORT ON TRACTOR HIRE PROGRAMME**

The Head of Operations, Alhaji Suleiman Garba, reported on the progress of the tractor hire programme for the year. He informed the Board that the Federation currently had nine tractors in service, of which seven were operational. Two tractors were undergoing major repairs at the Federation’s workshop in Kano and were expected to be back in service by mid-June.

**Observation by Malam Kabir Adamu:** In paragraph 7.2 of the previous minutes, the figure quoted for the fertiliser budget provision was stated as ₦35,000,000.00. Malam Kabir noted that the correct figure was ₦35,500,000.00, as per the revised budget approved at the Emergency Board Meeting of 10 December 2024.

**Action:** The minutes were corrected accordingly. Subject to that amendment, the minutes were approved as a true and accurate record of the previous meeting.

**Proposed by:** Alhaji Tijjani Yusuf
**Seconded by:** Mrs. Grace Okonkwo

According to the board resolution, the Kano River Basin Cooperative Federation audit_firm is Sahel Audit Associates. Record status: current.

---

## 4.0 MATTERS ARISING FROM THE PREVIOUS MINUTES

### 4.1 Appointment of Head of Planning
The Chairman confirmed that the letter of appointment for Hajiya Fatima Sani had been issued on 20 May 2024, well before the effective date of 1 June 2024. He further confirmed that Hajiya Fatima had completed her six-month probationary period satisfactorily and that her appointment had been confirmed with effect from 1 December 2024.

### 4.2 Fertiliser Procurement – Transport Contractors
The General Manager reported that the engagement of transport contractors for the movement of fertiliser from the central store to the zonal collection centres at Dambatta, Challawa, and Tudun Wada had been completed. The contracts were awarded to two firms: Malam Bala Transport Services (for the Dambatta and Challawa routes) and Kano Logistics Company Limited (for the Tudun Wada route). The total contract sum was ₦12,750,000.00, within the approved budget.

### 4.3 Tractor Hire Programme
The Head of Operations reported that the two tractors undergoing major repairs at the Federation’s workshop had been returned to service by mid-June 2024 as anticipated. All nine tractors were now operational. The programme had served 1,240 farmers during the 2024 farming season, generating gross revenue of ₦18,600,000.00.

---

## 5.0 FINANCIAL REVIEW – YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2024

The Treasurer, Malam Ibrahim Musa, presented the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024. He noted that the Federation had recorded a surplus of ₦48,250,000.00, compared with a surplus of ₦31,800,000.00 in the previous year. Income from fertiliser sales accounted for 62% of total revenue, while tractor hire contributed 18% and membership subscription fees contributed 12%.

The Treasurer drew the Board’s attention to two matters:

1. **Receivables:** An amount of ₦8,400,000.00 was outstanding from the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company in respect of the Federation’s commission on fertiliser sales. This amount had been on the books since September 2024. The Treasurer recommended that the General Manager write a formal reminder letter to the company.
## 6.0 CAPITAL EXPENDITURE AND BUDGET REVIEW

### 6.1 Capital Expenditure Report – First Half 2025

The Treasurer presented the capital expenditure report for the period 1 January to 30 June 2025. Total capital expenditure during the period amounted to ₦23,450,000.00, against a revised annual budget of ₦41,000,000.00. The main items of expenditure were:

| Item | Approved Budget (₦) | Actual Expenditure (₦) | Variance (₦) |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|--------------|
| Workshop equipment and tools | 6,500,000.00 | 5,850,000.00 | 650,000.00 |
| Office renovation (Headquarters) | 8,000,000.00 | 7,200,000.00 | 800,000.00 |
| IT equipment and software | 4,500,000.00 | 4,125,000.00 | 375,000.00 |
| Purchase of one pickup vehicle | 12,000,000.00 | 6,275,000.00 | 5,725,000.00 |
| **Total** | **41,000,000.00** | **23,450,000.00** | **17,550,000.00** |

The Treasurer explained that the purchase of the pickup vehicle had been delayed due to the unavailability of the preferred model from the authorised dealer. The General Manager reported that a deposit of ₦6,275,000.00 had been paid, and delivery was expected by September 2025. The Board noted that the remaining capital budget of ₦17,550,000.00 was earmarked for the completion of the workshop extension and the installation of a backup generator, both of which were scheduled for the third and fourth quarters.

**Decision 6.1.1:** The Board approved the capital expenditure incurred to date and authorised the General Manager to proceed with the remaining capital projects within the approved budget.

### 6.2 Revised Budget for 2025

The Treasurer presented a revised budget for the year ending 31 December 2025. The revision was necessary to reflect the increase in fertiliser prices announced by the Federal Government in May 2025 and the corresponding reduction in the volume of fertiliser expected to be allocated to the Federation by the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company.

The revised revenue budget was set at ₦215,000,000.00, compared with the original budget of ₦228,000,000.00. The reduction of ₦13,000,000.00 was attributed to an expected shortfall in fertiliser sales volume of approximately 20%. The revised expenditure budget was set at ₦186,500,000.00, compared with the original budget of ₦192,000,000.00, reflecting savings in transport costs and administrative expenses.

The Board discussed the revised budget at length. Malam Bello Abdullahi queried whether the Federation should consider sourcing fertiliser from alternative suppliers to make up the shortfall. The General Manager responded that the Federation had received an offer from a private supplier in Kaduna, but the price was 15% higher than the government-subsidised rate. After deliberation, the Board agreed that the Federation should continue to rely on the government allocation for the 2025 season and revisit the matter in 2026.

**Decision 6.2.1:** The Board approved the revised budget for the year ending 31 December 2025, as presented by the Treasurer.

## 7.0 COMMITTEE REPORTS

### 7.1 Audit Committee Report

The Chairman of the Audit Committee, Alhaji Suleiman Garba, presented the committee’s report for the half year ended 30 June 2025. The committee had reviewed the Federation’s internal controls and had found them to be generally satisfactory. However, the committee made the following recommendations:

1. That the Federation should reconcile its bank statements on a monthly basis, rather than quarterly, to reduce the risk of errors.
2. That the General Manager should ensure that all procurement above ₦500,000.00 is subject to competitive bidding, in line with the Federation’s procurement policy.
3. That the Federation should appoint an external auditor to conduct a mid-year review of the accounts, at an estimated cost of ₦350,000.00.
## 8.0 PROCUREMENT UPDATE

The General Manager presented an update on the Federation’s procurement activities for the third quarter of 2025. He reported that the Federation had completed the procurement of 1,200 bags of maize seed at a total cost of ₦18,600,000.00, which was within the budgeted amount. The seed had been distributed to member cooperatives in Kano, Jigawa, and Katsina States.

The General Manager further reported that the Federation had received quotations for the supply of 500 bags of NPK fertiliser from three suppliers. The quotations were as follows:

| Supplier | Price per bag (₦) | Delivery time |
|----------|-------------------|---------------|
| Kano Agro Supplies | 24,500.00 | 10 days |
| Northern Fertiliser Ltd | 25,200.00 | 7 days |
| Green Fields Nigeria | 26,000.00 | 5 days |

The Board considered the quotations. Malam Bello Abdullahi noted that while Green Fields Nigeria offered the fastest delivery, the price was significantly higher than the other two suppliers. The General Manager advised that the Federation did not require urgent delivery, as the fertiliser would not be needed until the planting season in May 2026. The Board therefore agreed to accept the quotation from Kano Agro Supplies, subject to confirmation that the fertiliser met the required quality standards.

**Decision 8.0.1:** The Board approved the procurement of 500 bags of NPK fertiliser from Kano Agro Supplies at ₦24,500.00 per bag, subject to quality verification.

The General Manager also reported that the Federation’s procurement policy required all purchases above ₦500,000.00 to be subject to competitive bidding. He confirmed that the procurement of maize seed had followed this procedure, with quotations obtained from three suppliers. The Board noted this with satisfaction.

## 9.0 ANNUAL PLAN FOR 2026

The General Manager presented a draft annual plan for the year 2026 for the Board’s consideration. The plan set out the following key targets:

1. An increase in membership from 1,850 to 2,100 member cooperatives.
2. The establishment of two new collection centres, one in Dutse and one in Hadejia.
3. A target of 12,000 metric tonnes of grain handled, compared with 9,500 metric tonnes in 2025.
4. The introduction of a farmer training programme, in partnership with the Kano State Agricultural Development Programme, expected to train 3,000 farmers.

The Board discussed the draft plan. Alhaji Suleiman Garba asked whether the Federation had the capacity to handle the increased volume of grain, given that the existing storage facilities were already operating at near capacity. The General Manager responded that the Federation had identified a warehouse in Dutse that could be leased, at an estimated cost of ₦4,500,000.00 per year, and that this would provide sufficient additional capacity.

The Treasurer noted that the cost of leasing the warehouse had not been included in the draft budget for 2026. The General Manager confirmed that this was an oversight and that the cost would be included in the revised budget, which would be presented to the Board at its next meeting.

**Decision 9.0.1:** The Board approved the draft annual plan for 2026 in principle, subject to the inclusion of the warehouse leasing cost in the revised budget and further review at the next meeting.

## 10.0 MEMBERSHIP SUBSCRIPTION FEES

The Board considered a proposal from the General Manager to increase membership subscription fees for 2026. The current fee was ₦5,000.00 per member cooperative per year. The General Manager proposed an increase to ₦7,500.00, citing rising administrative costs and the need to fund new initiatives under the annual plan.

**4.1** The Treasurer reported that the outstanding payment to the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company for the 2023 dry-season fertilizer order had been settled on 28 December 2023. The payment of ₦4,850,000.00 was made via bank transfer, and the receipt has been filed.

**4.2** The Secretary reported that letters of appreciation had been dispatched to the three cooperative societies that hosted the Board’s inspection visits in November 2023. No further action was required.

**4.3** The Chairman noted that the matter of the proposed borehole rehabilitation at the Dambatta collection centre had been deferred to this meeting for discussion under Item 7.0. There was no other business arising.

**5.0 CHAIRMAN’S REMARKS**

According to the board minutes, Ahmadu Bello appointment_date is 2024-01-15. Record status: current.

The Chairman welcomed members to the first Board meeting of the year. He noted that the 2024 farming season would be critical for the Federation, given the anticipated increase in the cost of inputs and the ongoing efforts to expand the Federation’s warehouse capacity. He urged members to consider the budget proposals for the year carefully and to prioritise programmes that would directly benefit member cooperatives.

**6.0 APPROVAL OF THE 2024 BUDGET**

The Treasurer presented the draft budget for the year ending 31 December 2024. He highlighted the following key figures:

- Total projected income: ₦128,650,000.00
- Total projected expenditure: ₦121,400,000.00
- Projected surplus: ₦7,250,000.00

The budget provided for an allocation of ₦35,000,000.00 for the procurement of fertiliser and improved seeds, ₦18,200,000.00 for the construction of a new warehouse at the Challawa centre, and ₦9,500,000.00 for the Federation’s tractor hire programme. The budget also made provision for administrative expenses of ₦12,750,000.00.

Members raised questions regarding the provision for staff training, which had been set at ₦1,500,000.00. The Treasurer explained that this amount was intended to cover two training workshops for cooperative extension officers. After discussion, the Board approved the budget as presented.

**Resolution 2024/01:** *That the budget for the year ending 31 December 2024, with total projected income of ₦128,650,000.00 and total projected expenditure of ₦121,400,000.00, be and is hereby approved.*

**7.0 REPORT ON THE DAMBATTA COLLECTION CENTRE BOREHOLE**

The General Manager, Ahmadu Bello, presented a verbal report on the condition of the borehole at the Dambatta collection centre. He informed the Board that the borehole had been non-functional since October 2023 due to a failed pump. A quotation for the replacement of the pump and associated works, in the sum of ₦2,350,000.00, had been obtained from a reputable contractor in Kano. The General Manager recommended that the work be carried out before the onset of the rainy season to ensure water availability for the cleaning of storage facilities.

**8.0 APPOINTMENT OF HEAD OF PLANNING**

The Chairman informed the Board that the position of Head of Planning, which had been vacant since the retirement of Alhaji Musa Ibrahim in March 2024, had been advertised internally and externally. He reported that the Interview Panel, chaired by the Vice-Chairman, had considered applications from eleven candidates and had shortlisted four for interview.

The Vice-Chairman presented the panel’s report. He stated that all four shortlisted candidates had been interviewed on 27 May 2024 and that the panel had assessed each candidate against the criteria of relevant experience, knowledge of cooperative law and practice, and familiarity with the Federation’s operational areas. After deliberation, the panel recommended the appointment of Fatima Sani, who had served as Senior Planning Officer in the Federation since 2019 and had acted as Head of Planning during the vacancy.

The Board discussed the recommendation at length. The Treasurer noted that Fatima Sani had demonstrated strong capability in preparing the 2024 budget submissions and in coordinating the Federation’s input distribution schedules. The General Manager supported the recommendation, stating that she had managed the planning unit effectively during the period of the vacancy and had maintained good working relationships with the zonal officers.

The board minutes state that Fatima Sani appointment_date is 2024-06-01. Record status: current. There being no further nominations, the Chairman put the matter to a vote.

**Resolution 2024/02:** *That Fatima Sani be and is hereby appointed as Head of Planning of the Kano River Basin Cooperative Federation with effect from 1 June 2024, subject to the satisfactory completion of a six-month probationary period.*

The Chairman congratulated the appointee and asked the General Manager to ensure that the necessary letter of appointment, including the terms and conditions of service, be issued before the effective date.

**9.0 OPERATIONAL UPDATE ON FERTILISER PROCUREMENT**

The General Manager reported that the Federation had received confirmation from the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company regarding the allocation of fertiliser for the 2024 farming season. The allocation comprised 1,200 metric tonnes of NPK 20:10:10 and 800 metric tonnes of urea. The total cost, including transport to the Federation’s central store in Kano, was estimated at ₦214,000,000.00, which was within the budget provision of ₦35,000,000.00 only in respect of the Federation’s own procurement share; the remainder was to be financed through the Central Bank of Nigeria’s commercial agricultural credit scheme, for which the Federation had already submitted the necessary documentation.

The General Manager further informed the Board that the disbursement of the loan was expected within three weeks. He recommended that the Federation proceed with the engagement of transport contractors for the movement of fertiliser from the central store to the zonal collection centres at Dambatta, Challawa, and Tudun Wada. The Board noted the update.

**10.0 REPORT ON TRACTOR HIRE PROGRAMME**

The Head of Operations, Alhaji Suleiman Garba, reported on the progress of the tractor hire programme for the year. He informed the Board that the Federation currently had nine tractors in service, of which seven were operational. Two tractors were undergoing major repairs at the Federation’s workshop in Kano and were expected to be back in service by mid-June.

The General Manager reported that the engagement of transport contractors for the movement of fertiliser from the central store to the zonal collection centres at Dambatta, Challawa, and Tudun Wada had been completed. ## 5.0 FINANCIAL REVIEW – YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2024

The Treasurer, Malam Ibrahim Musa, presented the audited financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024. He noted that the Federation had recorded a surplus of ₦48,250,000.00, compared with a surplus of ₦31,800,000.00 in the previous year. Income from fertiliser sales accounted for 62% of total revenue, while tractor hire contributed 18% and membership subscription fees contributed 12%.

The Treasurer drew the Board’s attention to two matters:

1. **Receivables:** An amount of ₦8,400,000.00 was outstanding from the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company in respect of the Federation’s commission on fertiliser sales. ## 6.0 CAPITAL EXPENDITURE AND BUDGET REVIEW

### 6.1 Capital Expenditure Report – First Half 2025

The Treasurer presented the capital expenditure report for the period 1 January to 30 June 2025. Total capital expenditure during the period amounted to ₦23,450,000.00, against a revised annual budget of ₦41,000,000.00. The main items of expenditure were:

| Item | Approved Budget (₦) | Actual Expenditure (₦) | Variance (₦) |
|------|---------------------|------------------------|--------------|
| Workshop equipment and tools | 6,500,000.00 | 5,850,000.00 | 650,000.00 |
| Office renovation (Headquarters) | 8,000,000.00 | 7,200,000.00 | 800,000.00 |
| IT equipment and software | 4,500,000.00 | 4,125,000.00 | 375,000.00 |
| Purchase of one pickup vehicle | 12,000,000.00 | 6,275,000.00 | 5,725,000.00 |
| **Total** | **41,000,000.00** | **23,450,000.00** | **17,550,000.00** |

The Treasurer explained that the purchase of the pickup vehicle had been delayed due to the unavailability of the preferred model from the authorised dealer. The General Manager reported that a deposit of ₦6,275,000.00 had been paid, and delivery was expected by September 2025. The Board noted that the remaining capital budget of ₦17,550,000.00 was earmarked for the completion of the workshop extension and the installation of a backup generator, both of which were scheduled for the third and fourth quarters.

**Decision 6.1.1:** The Board approved the capital expenditure incurred to date and authorised the General Manager to proceed with the remaining capital projects within the approved budget.

### 6.2 Revised Budget for 2025

The Treasurer presented a revised budget for the year ending 31 December 2025. The revision was necessary to reflect the increase in fertiliser prices announced by the Federal Government in May 2025 and the corresponding reduction in the volume of fertiliser expected to be allocated to the Federation by the Kano State Agricultural Supply Company.

The revised revenue budget was set at ₦215,000,000.00, compared with the original budget of ₦228,000,000.00. The reduction of ₦13,000,000.00 was attributed to an expected shortfall in fertiliser sales volume of approximately 20%. The revised expenditure budget was set at ₦186,500,000.00, compared with the original budget of ₦192,000,000.00, reflecting savings in transport costs and administrative expenses.

The Board discussed the revised budget at length. Malam Bello Abdullahi queried whether the Federation should consider sourcing fertiliser from alternative suppliers to make up the shortfall. The General Manager responded that the Federation had received an offer from a private supplier in Kaduna, but the price was 15% higher than the government-subsidised rate. After deliberation, the Board agreed that the Federation should continue to rely on the government allocation for the 2025 season and revisit the matter in 2026.

**Decision 6.2.1:** The Board approved the revised budget for the year ending 31 December 2025, as presented by the Treasurer.

## 7.0 COMMITTEE REPORTS

### 7.1 Audit Committee Report

The Chairman of the Audit Committee, Alhaji Suleiman Garba, presented the committee’s report for the half year ended 30 June 2025. The committee had reviewed the Federation’s internal controls and had found them to be generally satisfactory. However, the committee made the following recommendations:

1. That the Federation should reconcile its bank statements on a monthly basis, rather than quarterly, to reduce the risk of errors.
2. That the General Manager should ensure that all procurement above ₦500,000.00 is subject to competitive bidding, in line with the Federation’s procurement policy.
3. That the Federation should appoint an external auditor to conduct a mid-year review of the accounts, at an estimated cost of ₦350,000.00.

documents.content:
## 8.0 PROCUREMENT UPDATE

The General Manager presented an update on the Federation’s procurement activities for the third quarter of 2025. He reported that the Federation had completed the procurement of 1,200 bags of maize seed at a total cost of ₦18,600,000.00, which was within the budgeted amount. The seed had been distributed to member cooperatives in Kano, Jigawa, and Katsina States.

The General Manager further reported that the Federation had received quotations for the supply of 500 bags of NPK fertiliser from three suppliers. The quotations were as follows:

| Supplier | Price per bag (₦) | Delivery time |
|----------|-------------------|---------------|
| Kano Agro Supplies | 24,500.00 | 10 days |
| Northern Fertiliser Ltd | 25,200.00 | 7 days |
| Green Fields Nigeria | 26,000.00 | 5 days |

The Board considered the quotations. Malam Bello Abdullahi noted that while Green Fields Nigeria offered the fastest delivery, the price was significantly higher than the other two suppliers. The General Manager advised that the Federation did not require urgent delivery, as the fertiliser would not be needed until the planting season in May 2026. The Board therefore agreed to accept the quotation from Kano Agro Supplies, subject to confirmation that the fertiliser met the required quality standards.

**Decision 8.0.1:** The Board approved the procurement of 500 bags of NPK fertiliser from Kano Agro Supplies at ₦24,500.00 per bag, subject to quality verification.

The General Manager also reported that the Federation’s procurement policy required all purchases above ₦500,000.00 to be subject to competitive bidding. He confirmed that the procurement of maize seed had followed this procedure, with quotations obtained from three suppliers. The Board noted this with satisfaction.

## 9.0 ANNUAL PLAN FOR 2026

The General Manager presented a draft annual plan for the year 2026 for the Board’s consideration. The plan set out the following key targets:

1. An increase in membership from 1,850 to 2,100 member cooperatives.
2. The establishment of two new collection centres, one in Dutse and one in Hadejia.
3. A target of 12,000 metric tonnes of grain handled, compared with 9,500 metric tonnes in 2025.
4. The introduction of a farmer training programme, in partnership with the Kano State Agricultural Development Programme, expected to train 3,000 farmers.

The Board discussed the draft plan. Alhaji Suleiman Garba asked whether the Federation had the capacity to handle the increased volume of grain, given that the existing storage facilities were already operating at near capacity. The General Manager responded that the Federation had identified a warehouse in Dutse that could be leased, at an estimated cost of ₦4,500,000.00 per year, and that this would provide sufficient additional capacity.

The Treasurer noted that the cost of leasing the warehouse had not been included in the draft budget for 2026. The General Manager confirmed that this was an oversight and that the cost would be included in the revised budget, which would be presented to the Board at its next meeting.

**Decision 9.0.1:** The Board approved the draft annual plan for 2026 in principle, subject to the inclusion of the warehouse leasing cost in the revised budget and further review at the next meeting.

## 10.0 MEMBERSHIP SUBSCRIPTION FEES

The Board considered a proposal from the General Manager to increase membership subscription fees for 2026. The current fee was ₦5,000.00 per member cooperative per year. The General Manager proposed an increase to ₦7,500.00, citing rising administrative costs and the need to fund new initiatives under the annual plan.

**ARTICLE 13: DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

13.1 The parties shall use all reasonable endeavours to resolve any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Contract, including any question regarding its existence, validity, or termination, through good-faith negotiation. Either party may initiate this process by serving written notice of the dispute on the other party, and senior representatives of both parties shall meet within fourteen (14) days of such notice to attempt an amicable resolution.

13.2 If the dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of the initial notice, the parties shall refer the matter to mediation administered by the Lagos Court of Arbitration in accordance with its Mediation Rules in force at the time. The mediator shall be appointed by mutual agreement of the parties. Each party shall bear its own costs of mediation, and the costs of the mediator shall be shared equally.

13.3 Any dispute not resolved by negotiation or mediation within sixty (60) days of the initial notice may be referred by either party to arbitration. The arbitration shall be conducted in English in Abuja, Nigeria, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Cap A18, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, and any statutory modification or re-enactment thereof. The tribunal shall consist of a single arbitrator appointed by the Chairman of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators (Nigeria Branch). The award of the arbitrator shall be final and binding on both parties, and judgment upon the award may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction.

13.4 Notwithstanding the foregoing, nothing in this Article shall prevent either party from seeking urgent injunctive or other interim relief from a court of competent jurisdiction where such relief is necessary to protect its rights or property pending the resolution of the dispute.

**ARTICLE 14: TERMINATION**

14.1 The Agency may terminate this Contract by written notice to the Supplier, effective immediately, if the Supplier:

a) commits a material breach of any of its obligations under this Contract and fails to remedy such breach within thirty (30) days of receiving written notice requiring it to do so;

b) repeatedly breaches any of its obligations under this Contract in a manner that indicates a lack of intention or ability to perform;

c) becomes insolvent, is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, enters into any arrangement with its creditors, or has a receiver, administrator, or liquidator appointed over any part of its assets or undertaking; or

d) is found to have engaged in fraudulent, corrupt, or collusive practices in connection with the award or performance of this Contract.

14.2 The Supplier may terminate this Contract by written notice to the Agency, effective immediately, if the Agency fails to pay any undisputed amount due under this Contract within sixty (60) days of the due date and fails to remedy such failure within a further thirty (30) days of receiving written notice from the Supplier.

14.3 Either party may terminate this Contract for convenience by giving the other party not less than ninety (90) days’ prior written notice. In the event of termination for convenience by the Agency, the Agency shall pay the Supplier for all Fertiliser Products delivered and accepted up to the effective date of termination, together with all reasonable costs incurred by the Supplier in respect of the unperformed portion of the Contract, including but not limited to costs of raw materials, packaging, and storage, subject to the Supplier’s duty to mitigate such costs.
